title: Whole Grain Pasta with Cream Sauce and Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta is made from whole wheat flour, retaining the bran and germ. Combined with a creamy sauce and added vegetables, it creates a nutritious home‑cooked dish rich in fiber, vitamins, and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta keeps the bran and germ, boosting its nutritional value compared with refined white pasta.
Cream sauces are often based on dairy cream, milk, or soft cheese, giving the dish a silky texture.
Vegetables such as broccoli, carrots, and spinach increase the content of vitamins A, C, and K.
Home recipes allow control over salt and fat, making the meal healthier.
Whole grain pasta has a lower glycemic index than traditional refined‑flour pasta.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates deliver sustained energy and promote satiety.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from vegetables
items.content: Added vegetables contribute vitamin C, folate, potassium, and antioxidants, supporting immunity and heart health.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: A cream sauce made with low‑fat dairy or plant‑based alternatives supplies moderate amounts of mono‑ and polyunsaturated fats.

items.title: Plant‑based protein
items.content: Together, pasta and vegetables provide a decent amount of plant protein for tissue repair.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Whole grain pasta contains gluten, so people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should choose gluten‑free alternatives.

items.title: High calorie content in cream sauce
items.content: Cream can add significant calories and saturated fat; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Prepared sauces or added salt can raise sodium; it is better to make the sauce from scratch with minimal salt.

items.title: Food safety with improper storage
items.content: Leaving the cooked dish at room temperature can promote bacterial growth; refrigerate within two hours and consume within 2 days.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Cook whole grain pasta in salted boiling water until al dente (about 8‑10 minutes). In a skillet, sauté diced vegetables (broccoli, carrots, spinach) until tender, add cream, simmer until thickened, season with salt, pepper, and herbs. Toss the pasta with the sauce, serve hot, and optionally garnish with grated Parmesan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the finished pasta in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. Keep the cream sauce separate and reheat before serving. Frozen portions can be kept up to 1 month, though texture may change.
